b6_4_artifact_safety.method: Full production build with canary env: VITE_LOVABLE_API_KEY='lovable_sk_CANARY_MUST_NOT_LEAK_1234567890' and VITE_OMNIVERSE_HOST='canary-omni.internal.example', then string-scan dist/.

root_cause.code: const meta = (import.meta as unknown as { env?: Record<string, string | undefined> }).env;
root_cause.explanation: Bare access to `import.meta.env` (without a property lookup) causes Vite to inline the entire env object at build time, exposing every VITE_* value — including any secret the user or CI has set — as a plaintext string in the browser bundle.

b6_4_artifact_safety.severity: P0 — supersedes Checkpoint B2's 'secret purge complete' claim. Even after src/lib/llm/client.ts was neutered, the bundle continues to leak every VITE_* env var present at build time. The CI enforcer's rule #4 (grep for VITE_LOVABLE_API_KEY in src) does NOT catch this class of leak because there is no source-level reference — Vite generates the leak from the bundler side.
b6_4_artifact_safety.recommended_fix: Replace the bare `import.meta.env` read with a dedicated helper that only touches the named keys (`import.meta.env.VITE_OMNIVERSE_KIT_URL`, etc.). Add a bundle-side CI check that greps the built dist/ for any VITE_* key literal other than the three publicly-safe ones (VITE_SUPABASE_URL, VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, VITE_SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID).
